mismatch.message: C calls distfleeck() at the first differing RNG call; JavaScript consumes rnd(20) in resist_conflict().

summary: The first step-133 divergence is a missing post-attack cuss-check draw in JavaScript dochug(). C executes the Archon’s MS_CUSS gate after its gaze; the gate consumes rn2(5)=4. JavaScript omits that check under a D:1 random-generation assumption, but this case creates the Archon explicitly with #wizgenesis, which bypasses that cap. The matching rn2(5)=4 from the next Fire Giant distfleeck() masks the missing draw; at RNG index 2705, C is in the Fire Giant’s distfleeck() while JavaScript is already in its mon_allowflags() call from m_move(). The screen cell is the HP ones digit (C 3, JS 1); the full JavaScript HP was not captured.

source.branch: After PHASE FOUR, C dochug() consumes rn2(5) when the monster is in range, has MS_CUSS, is hostile, its square is couldsee-visible, and it is not invisible; it calls wizard.c:cuss() when the draw is zero. JavaScript omits this gate because it assumes D:1 difficulty prevents MS_CUSS species, but the assigned #wizgenesis recipe explicitly creates an Archon with MS_CUSS. This missing draw shifts the next monster’s movement and attack RNG order.

evidence: The current combined evaluation challenges/evaluations/20261003200023-v21.json at f6bd7d8b254913e53e05ca7fd0a7048eed7f8f34 reports 133/138 screens matched and 5 remaining. At segment 0, step 133, the first RNG difference is index 2705: C rn2(5)=1 from distfleeck(monmove.c:538), JavaScript rnd(20)=12. The screen mismatch at row 23, column 16 is the HP ones digit (C 3, JS 1), not the full HP; the C step output shows HP 143(148), and no full JavaScript HP value is claimed.

The saved C step-133 recording begins rnd(3)=3 at gazemu, rn2(5)=4 at dochug(monmove.c:992), rn2(5)=1 at distfleeck(monmove.c:538), then rnd(20)=20 at resist_conflict(mondata.c:1612). The step output says the Archon blinded the hero and then “It hits.” In current upstream, the dochug() rn2(5) source is the cuss gate at monmove.c:983-985; monsters.h defines Archon with MS_CUSS. The recipe creates a hostile Archon with #wizgenesis after creating the Fire Giant; read.c:create_particular_creation() uses the requested species directly when randmonst is false, bypassing the D:1 random-monster difficulty cap. The recorded cuss gate result is 4, so the cuss() body is not entered on this step.

JavaScript js/monmove.js:2403-2414 omits the cuss gate because its comment assumes D:1 cannot generate an MS_CUSS monster. dochug() then returns after PHASE FOUR at js/monmove.js:2771 without the C gate. In the exact-case inspector capture .cache/archon-v21-C66-resist-caller-probe-v3.json, the verified mondata.js breakpoint at RNG-log length 2705 identifies Fire Giant m_id 65 at (71,16), HP 52, in a planning clone; the call stack is resist_conflict -> mon_allowflags -> m_move -> moveSimpleOrdinary -> dochug. C therefore spends index 2704 on the Archon cuss gate and index 2705 on the Fire Giant distfleeck(), while JavaScript’s index-2704 rn2(5)=4 belongs to the Fire Giant’s earlier distanceAndFear()/distfleeck() call and index 2705 has already reached the Fire Giant’s mon_allowflags(). The equal value at index 2704 masks the skipped Archon draw.

C’s separate pre-dochug Conflict gate in mon.c:1305-1318 checks Conflict, !iswiz, m_canseeu(), cansee() of the monster square, and bolt range before fightm(). The current JavaScript live caller in js/allmain.js binds canSeeHero to () => true and then checks canSeeSquare in js/mon.js:1354-1367. The captured index-2705 call is later inside m_move()/mon_allowflags(), not fightm() or PHASE FOUR; the JavaScript m_canseeu-equivalent is true for that Fire Giant. The first cause is the earlier omitted cuss gate, not either Conflict attack gate.
